subject: Customer questions: training on customer data, log retention & DPIA evidence
messages:
From: Lara Shaw <privacy@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Question: training on customer conversations? logs & DPIA request

Marissa —

We're running a GDPR/third-party risk review ahead of a proof-of-concept with Redwood. A few quick questions so we can update our DPIA and vendor assessment. Please reply with short, actionable answers and any evidence you can share (SOC 2/SIG/CAIQ mappings, DPIA summary, sample logs).

1) Do you use customer prompts or responses to further train or fine-tune models (either hosted or internal product telemetry)? If so, are they identifiable or aggregated/anonymized?
2) How long do you retain raw prompts and model responses for hosted API customers by default? Is there a configuration to disable retention (opt-out) or to reduce retention to 0?
3) Do you persist embeddings derived from customer inputs? If so, where and for how long? Are embeddings reversible or considered personal data?
4) What controls do you have for preventing PII from persisting in logs? Do you perform automated redaction/scrubbing?
5) Can you provide (a) a short DPIA summary specific to processing customer conversational data, and (b) a small redacted sample of prompt/response logs and associated audit entries?

We'd like answers in the next 3 business days if possible so our security team can move forward.

Thanks —
Lara Shaw
Head of Privacy, FinBank Corp
privacy@finbank.com

Attachment: finbank-security-questionnaire-20261104.xlsx (xls)

- We'll attach a concise DPIA summary and redacted log sample.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: training on customer conversations? logs & DPIA request

Hi Lara —

Thanks — below are consolidated answers and references. I've kept each answer short and included where to find evidence. If you want, we can produce a FinBank-specific DPIA addendum that cites the clauses you need.

1) Training on customer data
- Hosted API (Redwood API): By default, we do not use customer prompts/responses to train or fine-tune the upstream model weights in a way that would make customer content part of model training. We may collect aggregate telemetry (e.g., token distribution, latency metrics) to improve service quality.
- Opt-in improvements: Customers may opt into an "aggregate, de-identified improvements" program; this is explicit, documented, and only available under a contract amendment. Any content included in that program is processed through de-identification, sampling, and review before any learning workflows.
- Dedicated & Private deployments: No customer data leaves the customer's environment for training. Private/VPC and on-prem installs have an explicit no-training guarantee unless the customer elects otherwise.

2) Retention of prompts/responses
- Default hosted retention: transient + short-term logs retained up to 30 days by default for troubleshooting, caching, and security telemetry.
- Opt-out / Zero retention: Customers can enable a "no-persist" mode at the account or request level which prevents long-term storage of prompts/responses; in this mode we keep ephemeral KV/cache in memory for the duration of the session only. This option is available on the hosted plan under standard commercial terms and as standard for Dedicated/Private.
- Deletion flow: We support an API-driven deletion request; for hosted accounts deletion of stored conversation materials is completed within 72 hours of the request with deletion audit entries in our tamper-evident logs.

3) Embeddings
- Persisting embeddings: We persist embeddings only when the customer enables features that require them (semantic search, similarity tooling). Storage is in the customer's tenant, encrypted at rest. Default retention follows the customer's configuration; many customers set the same retention window as other user data.
- Reversibility: Embeddings are not reversible to raw text in a practical, reliable manner under current techniques; however, depending on model and embedding size there is theoretical risk if combined with external knowledge. We therefore treat embeddings as potentially sensitive and recommend contract language that specifies handling and deletion requirements.

4) PII controls and redaction
- Automated detection: We offer optional automated PII detection hooks that can flag or redact items before persistence. This runs as a pre-processing pass at the tenant level and can be configured to block or mask.
- Post-ingest scrubbing: For hosted customers we can run scrubbers on stored logs as part of remediation/DSAR workflows; for Dedicated/Private customers scrubbers run inside the tenant.

5) Evidence and artifacts
- Attached: redwood-dpia-summary.pdf (short DPIA covering conversational data handling) and sample-prompt-log-redacted.txt (minimal, redacted example with corresponding audit entries).
- SOC 2 / SIG: We maintain a current SOC 2 Type II report; a mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls is available on request. See redwood-soc2-sig-links.txt (attached) for direct links.

Technical notes (brief)
- KV cache: We use an in-memory KV cache for decoding performance; cache entries are ephemeral and, unless the customer has longer retention enabled for debugging, not persisted to long-term storage.
- Encryption: All customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Customers on Redwood Private or Dedicated can supply KMS keys (SSE-KMS/HSM) for envelope encryption.
- Auditability: Deletion, access, and config changes are recorded in immutable audit logs with retention aligned to the customer's contract.

Next steps
- I can prepare a one-page DPIA addendum that we can sign and attach to your vendor file.
- If you want deeper technical evidence, we can arrange a short session with our product security engineer to walk through redaction hooks and sample logs.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: redwood-dpia-summary.pdf (pdf); sample-prompt-log-redacted.txt (txt); redwood-soc2-sig-links.txt (txt)

Subject: Re: Question: training on customer conversations? logs & DPIA request

Neha / Marissa —

Appreciate the detailed rundown. A couple of follow-ups from our security/engineering side:

1) Redaction: In the redacted sample you provided we still saw tokens like "<NAME_REDACTED>". Do you ever retain raw PII in a separate staging area before redaction? If so, how long and who can access it?

2) PII detection accuracy: do you run multiple detectors (regex + ML classifiers) or a single rule set? We'd like to understand false positive/negative characteristics for removal hooks.

3) Embeddings: for the semantic search use-case — if we upload a customer corpus and ask Redwood to build an index, where are the stored vectors kept (which region/tenant) and what KMS options exist?

4) Contracting: can you provide proposed contract language (no-training clause, data deletion SLA, right to audit / evidence delivery cadence)?

If you can share language snippets we can circulate with procurement.

Thanks —
Daniel Cho
Senior Security Engineer, FinBank Corp

Daniel / Lara —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Below are suggested contract clauses and short answers to the engineering questions. Happy to convert these to a legal addendum for signature.

Suggested language (high-level snippets)
1) No-training clause:
"Supplier shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any underlying model weights, embeddings, or other machine learning assets used across Supplier's hosted services, except where expressly permitted in a written amendment signed by both parties."

2) Data retention & deletion SLA:
"Supplier will retain Customer Data only for the minimum period necessary for service delivery (default 30 days). Upon Customer request, Supplier will remove Customer Data from production and backup stores within 72 hours and provide audit evidence of deletion within 10 business days."

3) Embeddings & search index handling:
"Embeddings generated from Customer Data will be considered Customer Data. Supplier will store embeddings in the Customer's tenant/namespace and apply Customer-supplied KMS keys if so configured. Supplier will not use embeddings for model training."

Answers to engineering items
- Raw PII staging: We do not retain raw PII in separate long-term staging areas for hosted customers. Short-lived staging buffers used in processing may transiently hold raw data in memory, but those buffers are not written to long-term storage unless retention is enabled for debugging; access is restricted to a handful of engineers under MFA and privileged access controls and all access is logged.
- Detection stack: We run a layered approach — deterministic rules (regex) plus ML-based classifiers and keyword heuristics. Customers can tune thresholds for their tenant and opt into stricter blocking.
- Embedding storage region/tenant: Embeddings are stored in the tenant's region we scope at account creation (we can confirm the exact AWS/GCP region for FinBank in the follow-up). KMS: we support customer-supplied keys for Dedicated/Private and offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for certain hosted plans.

Next step: Marissa — can you propose two times for a legal + security call next week? We'll prepare a one-page addendum and the SOC2/SIG mapping for delivery.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
